land.text: Tunis, where the mutinous army made its base

predecessors.note: The rebels were Carthage's own unpaid mercenaries from the Sicilian war, joined by Libyan towns and Numidians; 'Rebel coins read from the Libyans'.

land.text: Tunis, Utica, Hippo and Leptis Parva, retaken by Hamilcar Barca

successors.note: 'Most towns that had not already submitted returned to Carthage and were treated leniently, though Carthaginian governors were imposed.'

capitals.name: Tunis
capitals.note: The rebel base: the mutineers marched on Tunis, fell back to it in early 238, and Hamilcar besieged it in late 238. No page calls it a capital.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -241..-240: Tunis and its district, the rebels' base. 'Spendius and Matho were declared generals' in late 241 and the army marched on Tunis; Matho's army was at Tunis (Hamilcar Barca page), and the rebels 'held the hills to the west of Carthage'. In early 240 they had blockaded Utica and Hippo without holding them. The page gives no boundary; a 40 km radius stands for the base.

correction.text: Tunis and the hills west of Carthage

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -239..-238: 'Utica and Hippo killed their Carthaginian garrisons and joined the rebels' between March and September 239; the page says the rebels controlled Utica, Hippo and Leptis Parva and 'operated around Carthage and Tunis', and does not date Leptis Parva's rising. 'Many towns rose' and '70,000 more men joined', but the page names no other town or region, so the rebel land is a minimum drawn from the four named places.

correction.text: Tunis, Utica, Hippo and Leptis Parva

ledger.note: Late 241 BC: Carthage's mercenaries mutiny. A dispute over wages owed to about 20,000 foreign soldiers from Sicily 'turned into a mutiny'; the mutineers seized Gisco and his treasury, and 'Spendius and Matho were declared generals'. Rebel coins read 'from the Libyans'. The page does not date their entry into Tunis.
Late 241 BC: the rebels hold Tunis. The mutineers moved to Sicca Veneria and 'later marched on Tunis'; Matho's army was at Tunis (Hamilcar Barca page).

239 BC: Utica and Hippo join the rebels. Between March and September 239 'Utica and Hippo killed their Carthaginian garrisons and joined the rebels'; Rome declined Utica's offer of the city. Leptis Parva, 'which had risen against Carthage earlier in the war' (page; no year), is added here so that the gain matches the -239 keyframe and the -238 loss (reviewer af-02-a); confidence 2 because its rising is undated.

region.text: Utica and Hippo (Bizerte), and Leptis Parva (Lamta)

ledger.note: 238 BC: Hamilcar Barca crushes the revolt. After the Battle of the Saw and the siege of Tunis, 'The Battle of Leptis Parva destroyed the remaining rebel army' and Matho was captured; Utica and Hippo surrendered 'late 238 or very early 237 BC' (Hamilcar Barca page: the revolt was over 'by the winter of 238 BC').

region.text: Tunis, Utica, Hippo and Leptis Parva

ledger.note: 238 BC: the rebellion ends. Spendius and his lieutenants were captured at the Saw and Matho at Leptis Parva (he was 'later tortured to death'); 'Most towns that had not already submitted returned to Carthage', with Carthaginian governors imposed. Carthage had to pay Rome 1,200 talents more after Rome seized Sardinia and Corsica (probably 237).

wars.name: Mercenary War

zones.text: Tunis, Utica, Hippo and Leptis Parva

wars.outcome: Hamilcar Barca won at the Bagradas, the Saw and Leptis Parva and the rebels were destroyed; Carthage recovered Utica, Hippo, Tunis and the Libyan towns. The war cost Carthage Sardinia, whose garrisons mutinied in 240-239.
wars.note: The Ancient Carthage page dates the war 241-237; the Hamilcar Barca page has the revolt over by the winter of 238. Naravas, a Numidian leader, defected to Carthage with 2,000 cavalry in 240.

certainty.note: The rebels held places, not frontiers; no page gives an extent beyond the cities named.

sources.title: Mercenary War
sources.note: The 241-238 revolt: Tunis, Utica, Hippo, Leptis Parva, the dates of the garrison revolts and the end of the war.

sources.title: Hamilcar Barca
sources.note: The rebels in the hills west of Carthage, Matho's army at Tunis, Utica and Hippo Acra in 239, the end in the winter of 238.

notes:
WHY A DOSSIER: the Mercenary War rebels held Tunis for about three years and Utica and Hippo for a year or more (rule 5: rebel-held land takes its own hatched colour); Cliopatria lacks them and the Carthage dossier (af-02-a) cites them as counterpart of its 241, 239 and 238 events. Slug from the name 'Mercenary rebels'.
WHAT IS NOT KNOWN: the extent of the Libyan revolt. The page says 'Many towns rose' and that 'Most towns that had not already submitted returned to Carthage', and names only Tunis, Utica, Hippo and Leptis Parva; Sicca Veneria, where the mutineers were moved, is a staging place. The shape is therefore a minimum. A gap-filler could open Polybius's account via a page that cites it.
DATES: Utica and Hippo went over in March-September 239; Leptis Parva is undated; surrender 'late 238 or very early 237'. The Ancient Carthage page's 241-237 range includes the Sardinian question that Rome settled in 237 (the Carthage dossier carries Sardinia and Corsica).
GAZETTEER: Tunis resolves; Utica, Hippo (Bizerte) and Leptis Parva (Lamta) are given by coordinates and need entries.
